chunks: A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from al-Naḍr ibn Suwayd, from Yaḥyā al-Ḥalabī, from ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd al-Ṭāʾī, from Yaʿqūb ibn Shuʿayb, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbdِ اللَّهِ عليه السلام about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:
“Work; so Allah will see your deeds, and His Messenger, and the believers.”
He عليه السلام said: “They are the Imams.”

key_terms.الْأَئِمَّةُ: the Imams, the designated guides in Shia doctrine
key_terms.الْمُؤْمِنُونَ: the believers, interpreted here as the Imams عليهم السلام
key_terms.فَسَيَرَى: then He will see; indicating observation of deeds
key_terms.قَوْلِ اللَّهِ: the statement or verse of Allah being asked about

ai.seo_question: Who are “the believers” in the verse “Work; so Allah will see your deeds, and His Messenger, and the believers”?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the Qur’anic phrase “and the believers” as referring specifically to the Imams عليهم السلام. It indicates, in Shia understanding, that the deeds of people are shown to Allah, His Messenger صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, and the Imams عليهم السلام.
